title: Mask state read across a @vf boundary, and exclusive prefix counts
surface: set_mask_by_count(n) / set_mask(0, pattern) / reset_mask() at kernel scope with move_mask_spr(mask) reading them inside a @vf; unsqueeze(reg, mask) replacing a register with the exclusive prefix count of a predicate
study_for: Mask state crosses the vector-function boundary, and that is the whole point of the `spr` mode. `set_mask_by_count` and `set_mask` are called at kernel scope; `move_mask_spr` reads the result inside the `@vf`. Each observation is rendered as 7-or-0 per lane and published before the next mask is installed, so three rows read in sequence say what the state was at three moments -- the third one, with nothing set, is the check that `reset_mask` put the full mask back.

Two SPR spellings that are not interchangeable. A count sets a prefix; a pattern sets arbitrary bits. `spr_20` pairs count 20 with pattern 0xF0F -- four set, four clear, four set -- which no count can produce, and that is what makes the pair of rows a comparison rather than a repetition. `spr_1`'s pattern has only bit 0 and bit 63, so a read that lost or sign-extended the high half of the 64-bit word fails at one lane on each end.

`unsqueeze` is an exclusive prefix count, and neither of the two things its name suggests. It replaces the register's contents with the number of earlier active lanes -- not including the lane itself -- so it is not a host reshape and not a decompaction of data values. `prefix_last`, where only lane 63 is active and every lane including that one answers zero, is the case that pins the word 'exclusive' down.

Both prefix rows run the same predicate over different old register contents (the second row's data is offset by 234567). They must agree. That is how the unit states that the old value is ignored, instead of trusting that it is -- and it costs one extra row.

Three of the ten cases have all-zero expected output (`spr_0`'s first two rows, `prefix_empty`, `prefix_last`), so a zero-filled destination would let a missing publication pass. The destination arrives at -777 for exactly that reason, and the sidecar controls in the pytest tree use perturbation and an inclusive-prefix comparison for those cases rather than a zero replacement that proves nothing there.
do_not_copy_when: You wanted an inclusive prefix. This is exclusive: lane `i` answers how many lanes before `i` were active. Adding the lane's own predicate back is your arithmetic, not the instruction's.
You expect `unsqueeze` to move data. It does not touch the values -- it overwrites the register with counts. A decompaction of the data itself is a gather or a scatter, not this.

You are setting a temporary mask and not resetting it. `spr_64` is the case where forgetting would still pass, because there the temporary mask and the full mask are the same. Every other case would catch it, and so would whatever ran after your kernel.
